title: The World Before Islam
Arabia and the Late Antique World
claims_to_verify: The chronology and dating of late antique Arabian settlements and trade networks.
The religious diversity of the Arabian Peninsula before Islam.
The historical evidence for Byzantine and Sasanian influence in the region.
The dating and interpretation of South Arabian inscriptions.
The historical context of Mecca and western Arabian trade before Islam.

scenes.narration: Before the rise of Islam, the world was already connected by powerful kingdoms, ancient trade routes, religious communities and remarkable cities. Arabia stood between several of these worlds.
scenes.visual_query: Arabian Peninsula Middle East physical relief map historical geography
scenes.source_notes: Opening geographical overview. Use a map rather than an imagined historical scene.

scenes.narration: To the west stood the Byzantine Empire, heir to the eastern Roman world. Its cities, churches, trade networks and political influence shaped the eastern Mediterranean.
scenes.visual_query: Byzantine late antique architecture mosaic church archaeological site
scenes.source_notes: Use surviving architecture or museum mosaics as evidence of the period.

scenes.narration: To the east, the Sasanian Persian Empire ruled a powerful realm. Its influence extended across Mesopotamia and parts of the lands surrounding Arabia.
scenes.visual_query: Sasanian Persian silver coin museum collection late antiquity
scenes.source_notes: Use an authenticated coin or museum artefact, not a fabricated royal portrait.

scenes.narration: Between these great powers were smaller kingdoms and communities. Their alliances, conflicts and trade helped connect Arabia with the wider region.
scenes.visual_query: Late antique Near East historical map Byzantine Sasanian frontier
scenes.source_notes: A historical map can communicate political geography without inventing a battle scene.

scenes.narration: Arabia itself was not an empty desert. It contained settled towns, agricultural areas, pastoral communities and important routes linking the Mediterranean, Africa and Asia.
scenes.visual_query: Hegra Mada'in Salih Nabataean archaeological settlement Saudi Arabia
scenes.source_notes: Use archaeological remains to show settlement and regional diversity.

scenes.narration: In the north, the Nabataeans left remarkable evidence of their skill in architecture and trade. Their rock-cut monuments at Petra and Hegra still survive.
scenes.visual_query: Petra Jordan Nabataean rock cut architecture archaeological site

scenes.narration: In southern Arabia, kingdoms such as Saba and Himyar developed centres of power. Inscriptions, buildings and other remains help historians study their societies.
scenes.visual_query: ancient South Arabian Sabaean inscription stone museum
scenes.source_notes: Use actual inscriptions and archaeological objects. Avoid treating every inscription as belonging to the same century.

scenes.narration: The south was also connected to the valuable trade in frankincense and other goods. Caravans and maritime routes carried products across the region.
scenes.visual_query: ancient frankincense trade incense burner archaeological museum Arabia
scenes.source_notes: Use museum artefacts related to incense and trade.

scenes.narration: Across the Red Sea, Arabia was connected to northeast Africa. Ships and ports helped move people, goods and ideas between neighbouring regions.
scenes.visual_query: Red Sea ancient maritime trade route historical map Arabia Africa
scenes.source_notes: Prefer a map or archaeological port evidence. Avoid unsupported depictions of particular voyages.

scenes.narration: Religion was also diverse. Jewish communities lived in parts of Arabia, Christian communities were present in several regions, and many people followed local polytheistic traditions.
scenes.visual_query: late antique Arabian Peninsula Jewish Christian religious archaeology inscription
scenes.source_notes: Use relevant inscriptions, buildings or material evidence. Avoid suggesting all communities shared one belief.

scenes.narration: In the south, the Himyarite kingdom experienced important religious changes. In the north and surrounding regions, Christian communities were linked to wider networks of worship and learning.
scenes.visual_query: late antique Himyarite South Arabian inscription Jewish history Yemen
scenes.source_notes: The chronology and interpretation of Himyarite religious history require careful sourcing.

scenes.narration: The desert also shaped daily life. Water sources, seasonal movement and knowledge of the land were essential for communities travelling across difficult terrain.
scenes.visual_query: Arabian desert oasis ancient settlement archaeological landscape
scenes.source_notes: Use real landscapes and archaeological sites, not staged images presented as historical photographs.

scenes.narration: Poetry and oral traditions held an important place in Arabian society. Language, memory, family ties and tribal relationships helped preserve identity and reputation.
scenes.visual_query: pre Islamic Arabic poetry manuscript Arabic calligraphy historical manuscript
scenes.source_notes: Surviving manuscripts may be later copies. Do not label a later manuscript as a contemporary pre-Islamic document.

scenes.narration: Mecca, in western Arabia, was associated with the Kaaba and pilgrimage traditions. The details of its early history are discussed through religious reports and historical scholarship.
scenes.visual_query: Masjid al Haram Kaaba historical architecture archival photograph
scenes.source_notes: Use respectful architectural imagery. Do not depict Prophet Muhammad ﷺ or claim that a modern photograph shows the pre-Islamic city.

scenes.narration: The wider world was changing through political rivalry, religious debate, commerce and cultural exchange. Arabia was part of this connected landscape, not separate from it.
scenes.visual_query: late antique world map Byzantine Sasanian Arabia trade routes
scenes.source_notes: Use a historically grounded map with clear period attribution.

scenes.narration: This was the world into which Islam would emerge in the seventh century. Understanding its geography, societies and beliefs helps us understand the historical setting of the beginning of Islam.
